title: The Free Kick That Turned Into a Spiral
coreQuestion: Why did Roberto Carlos's 1997 free kick against France bend so late?

lines.text: This free kick was flying wide. Then it turned.
Roberto Carlos hit it with the outside of his left foot, from far out.
The ball swung around the wall and kept heading wide.
Then it bent back in, past a goalkeeper who never moved.
Spin pushes the ball sideways. Drag slows the ball down, but the spin keeps going.
So the slower it flies, the tighter it curves, into a spiral.
That is why the bend came so late. Every goal has a story.

facts.claim: Roberto Carlos scored a free kick for Brazil against France on 3 June 1997 at the Stade de Gerland in Lyon, in the opening match of the Tournoi de France, which ended 1-1.
facts.source: Wikipedia, 1997 Tournoi de France; Sky Sports (skysports.com/football/news/11095/10899358)

facts.claim: He struck the ball with the outside of his left foot from long range; reported distances vary from about 33 metres to 40 yards.
facts.source: What A Howler; Sky Sports; Chalkdust Magazine

facts.claim: The ball swerved around the French wall and appeared to be heading wide before bending back into the goal.
facts.source: Sky Sports; What A Howler; ESPN

facts.claim: France goalkeeper Fabien Barthez did not move as the ball went in.
facts.source: What A Howler (single outlet in search; re-check)

facts.claim: In 2010 Guillaume Dupeux, Anne Le Goff, David Quere and Christophe Clanet published 'The spinning ball spiral' in New Journal of Physics 12, 093004.

The paper shows that a spinning ball slowed by drag, while its spin stays nearly constant, follows a path that curves more and more tightly, a spiral; the authors use Roberto Carlos's 1997 free kick as the example of a ball that began to follow this spiral.
facts.source: ScienceDaily; Physics World; APS DFD 2009 abstract 'The Roberto Carlos Spiral'

facts.claim: Model used for the animated trajectories: point ball with quadratic drag (Cd 0.25) and Magnus lift from the spin ratio, integrated with RK4; launch values are chosen for the illustration, not measured from the 1997 kick.
